note: 'He took the gold from their hands, and with an engraving tool he fashioned it into a molten calf.' (Exod 32:4). His own account at 32:24 is shorter: 'out came this calf!'.
'Come, make us gods who will go before us. As for this Moses who brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him!' (Exod 32:1).

'And God spoke all these words:' (Exod 20:1). At 34:28 the writing is Moses's hand -- 'He wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant' -- while 34:1 has the Lord say 'I will write on them'. **The text says both and the graph keeps both verses.**
'Then the LORD passed in front of Moses and called out' (Exod 34:6) -- the proclamation is his own, about himself, to Moses.
'Whoever is for the LORD, come to me. And all the Levites gathered around him' (Exod 32:26), and what follows at 32:27-28 is not softened by the text.
'you have led them into so great a sin' (Exod 32:21), after breaking the tables at the sight of the calf and the dancing (32:19).
